newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK economy to be unchanged after handover - Tung.
newsitem.headline: HK economy to be unchanged after handover - Tung.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa reassured world finance leaders on Friday that the territory's prosperous economic climate would remain unchanged after China takes over in July.

"As Chief Executive of the SAR (Special Administrative Region), I promise you that we will ensure that a free and fair ...and encouraging economic environment, the hallmark of Hong Kong, will be maintained," he told an International Monetary Fund conference.
"You will be able to see for yourself that the dynamics of the free market in Hong Kong has not and will not change."

Last December, the shipping magnate was picked by a China-controlled panel as the territory's chief executive to govern Hong Kong after it reverts to Beijing control on July 1, ending more than 150 years of British colonial rule.

"I wish to take this opportunity to impress upon you of my confidence that the transition will be smooth and the Hong Kong prosperity and way of life will be preserved way into the 21st Century," Tung said.
Hong Kong, a territory of 6.4 million people, reverts to China under a 1984 Sino-British treaty.
The treaty, the Joint Declaration, guarantees the territory will have a high degree of autonomy and keep its freewheeling capitalism for a further 50 years after the handover.
Hong Kong's people are among the richest in the world. Their hard toil in recent decades has created an enviable economic success story.
But there are fears that personal freedoms, the rule of law and democracy here will be eroded after Beijing takes over.

"Article 109 of the Basic Law requires the government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to provide the economic and legal environment to remain as an international financial centre. As Chief Executive of SAR, I pledge that I will uphold this continuity," Tung said.
The Basic Law is the territory's post-colonial constitution.

"Hong Kong's success has been as a result of a free and competitive economic environment with conservative fiscal policy, a simple tax system, a low tax rate, the rule of law, free enterprise, free trade, minimal corruption and bureaucracy and a level playing field provided and supported by an efficient civil service. And this will continue," Tung said.
The future government should provide personal freedom to make sure the people were proud to be part of the community so as to ensure sustained and stable economic growth, he said.
"We need to reaffirm our commitment to preserve the rule of law, our lifestyle," he added.
